project_name: Wearable Sleep Staging on PhysioNet BIDSLab

experiments.hypothesis: Real-data SleepChannelNet graph attention will outperform supervised baselines; SleepJEPA pretraining will enhance representations.
experiments.research_question: Can graph neural networks and self-supervised learning improve wearable sleep staging?
experiments.change: Baseline SleepChannelNet implementation with 10-node complete graph and SleepJEPA pretraining.
experiments.review: SleepJEPA negative result documented; supervised graph network provided strong baseline.

experiments.hypothesis: Official SLAMSS-IFS architecture from author repo can be faithfully reproduced with bitwise determinism.
experiments.research_question: Does the published SLAMSS-IFS paper match the author code repository?
experiments.change: Independent scientific reproduction audit against BIDSLabUMass/SLAMSS-IFS official repo.
experiments.reason: Verified exact baseline code and disclosed 5.47M parameter architectural divergence.
experiments.review: Reproducibility confirmed on hardware; paper model (666k) diverges from repo model (5.47M).

experiments.hypothesis: A compact dual-branch CNN with dynamic reliability gating, BiGRU context, GRL, and boundary loss can match SLAMSS-IFS with ~33x fewer parameters.
experiments.research_question: Can modular architectural mechanisms replace brute-force model bloat?
experiments.change: Implemented SleepAdaptiveNet (A0-A5, ~162k parameters) with switchable ablation toggles.
experiments.reason: All gradient flow and tensor shapes verified under 162,325 parameter budget.
experiments.review: Clean modular implementation; unit tests pass.

experiments.hypothesis: Dynamic reliability gating and GRL subject invariance will enhance validation Macro-F1 across 10 screening epochs.
experiments.research_question: Which proposed SleepAdaptiveNet components provide the largest early gains?
experiments.change: 10-epoch screening ablation of A0 through A5 on seed 42.
experiments.reason: GRL subject invariance doubled REM F1 (0.181 -> 0.361) and improved Macro-F1.
experiments.review: Early evidence of GRL utility; boundary loss requires GRL stabilization.

experiments.hypothesis: Boundary loss lambda=0.20 provides optimal trade-off between boundary error reduction and Wake recall.
experiments.research_question: What is the optimal Pareto boundary loss weight without degrading primary accuracy?
experiments.change: Boundary loss sweep lambda in {0.0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.50} with unconfounded GRL isolation.
experiments.reason: GRL standalone verified +3.21% accuracy gain; lambda=0.50 rejected due to Wake recall dip.
experiments.review: B0_GRL (lambda=0) and B2 (lambda=0.20) identified as lead candidates.

experiments.hypothesis: B0_GRL is stably superior to B2 across multiple random seeds.
experiments.research_question: Does B0_GRL maintain performance across independent random seeds 42, 123, 2024?
experiments.change: Multi-seed evaluation of B0_GRL vs B2 across 3 random seeds.
experiments.reason: B0_GRL consistently beat B2 on all 3 seeds by +0.75% Acc and +0.0115 Macro-F1.
experiments.review: B0_GRL locked as lead candidate for convergence studies.

experiments.hypothesis: Long training will allow B0_GRL to converge past 70% validation accuracy and resolve REM under-fitting.
experiments.research_question: At what epoch does B0_GRL converge, and does overfitting occur beyond 100 epochs?
experiments.reason: Demonstrated sharp convergence peak at Epoch 78-80; revealed severe overfitting beyond epoch 100.
experiments.review: Crucial finding: locked 80-epoch training budget for subsequent benchmarks.

experiments.hypothesis: The 80-epoch convergence peak is robust across seeds 42, 123, 2024.
experiments.research_question: Is the optimal convergence window stable across multiple random seeds?
experiments.change: Multi-seed 500-epoch runs across seeds 42, 123, 2024; bitwise RNG discrepancy audit.
experiments.reason: Confirmed optimal stopping window at exactly 80 epochs across 100% of seeds.
experiments.review: RNG discrepancy resolved; 80 epochs established as frozen budget.

experiments.hypothesis: Frozen SleepAdaptiveNet (B0_GRL) will generalize to the completely held-out official 11-subject test set.
experiments.research_question: Does SleepAdaptiveNet achieve competitive performance on held-out test subjects under 33.7x parameter compression?
experiments.change: Final frozen test benchmark of B0_GRL across 3 seeds on 34,241 valid test windows.
experiments.reason: Classified as Case B: Approximate Parity under 33.7x compression compared to 5.47M SLAMSS-IFS.
experiments.review: Frozen evaluation executed with zero test tuning or leakage.

experiments.hypothesis: SleepAdaptiveNet mechanisms provide measurable benefits beyond an approximately matched-capacity conventional CNN-BiGRU baseline.
experiments.research_question: What is the single-component performance attribution of GRL, Adaptive Fusion, and Transitions?
experiments.change: OFAT factorial ablation on test partition comparing Models A, B, C, D against frozen reference Model E.
experiments.reason: Model E outperformed Model A by +1.79% Acc [95% CI: +0.52%, +3.35%]; GRL was primary contributor (+1.39%).
experiments.review: Component attribution established on official test partition.

experiments.hypothesis: The performance benefits of SleepAdaptiveNet mechanisms generalize robustly across all 47 subjects in 5-fold cross-validation.
experiments.research_question: Does SleepAdaptiveNet consistently outperform matched baseline across diverse subject cohorts?
experiments.change: 75-run 5-fold cross-validation across all 47 subjects (5 models x 5 folds x 3 seeds).
experiments.reason: Established Scientific Outcome B: Equivalence / Parity. Inter-subject variance (ICC=0.963) dominates performance.
experiments.review: Comprehensive 75-run cross-validation demonstrates that matched-capacity models perform equivalently across random subject folds.

experiments.hypothesis: Removing the all-zero 'clock' feature from x_meta will not degrade Macro-F1 and will reduce input dimension by 1.
experiments.research_question: RQ-001: Does removing the dummy zero-placeholder clock feature impact baseline performance?
experiments.change: Prune all-zero clock channel from x_meta (4 meta channels instead of 5)
experiments.reason: Statistically meaningful Macro-F1 improvement (+0.1029) under matched capacity.
experiments.review: Scientific Review Verdict: ACCEPT (10/10 checks passed). All 10 experimental validity checks PASSED.
